paragraphs.text: Five or six years afore it happened. God loveth to foresignify, to forewarn, or ere he punish. Let us, upon whom the ends of the world are come, take warning, and think we hear the trump of God sounding as here, "An end is come, is come, is come; it watcheth for thee, behold it is come." {Eze 7:2-3; Eze 7:6}
paragraphs.anchor: Moreover the word of the Lord came unto me.

paragraphs.text: Exitium et excidium. Great kingdoms have their times and their turns, their rise and their ruin. The wicked’s happiness will take its end, surely and swiftly.
paragraphs.anchor: An end, the end is come.

paragraphs.text: Heb., The four wings, called also the "four winds." {Mat 24:31} They had defiled the land from corner to corner; {as Ezr 9:11} God therefore now would sweep it all over with the besom of utter destruction.
paragraphs.anchor: Upon the four corners of the land.

paragraphs.text: Even upon thee, O Israel. Who would ever have thought it {Lam 4:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Now is the end come upon thee.

paragraphs.text: Reveal it from heaven. {as Rom 1:18}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will send mine anger upon thee.

paragraphs.text: i.e., I will punish thee for thy ways. {as Hos 4:9 Oba 1:15}
paragraphs.anchor: And will judge thee according to thy ways

paragraphs.text: Heb., I will give or put upon thee all thine abominations - q.d., Thou hast hitherto put them upon me, but I will have a writ of removal, and set them upon their own base. {as Zec 5:11}
paragraphs.anchor: And will recompense upon thee.

paragraphs.text: Eze 5:11. See on Jer 13:14.
paragraphs.anchor: And mine eye shall not spare thee.

paragraphs.text: Ut quae antea latuerant, in aperture prodeant.
paragraphs.anchor: And thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee.

paragraphs.text: That smiteth you. {Eze 7:9}
paragraphs.anchor: And ye shall know that I am the Lord.

paragraphs.text: viz., Without mixture of mercy, or that shall smite thee down at one only blow. {as 1Sa 26:8 Nah 1:9} The Vulgate, after the Chaldee, rendereth it, An evil after an evil - q.d., Lighter and lesser judgments have done no good upon thee. Now I will finish the work, and cut it short in righteousness. {Rom 9:28} Ruinam praecedunt stillicidia. Drops precede disaster.
paragraphs.anchor: An evil, an only evil

paragraphs.text: Still the prophet ringeth this doleful knell in their ears, whom sin and Satan had cast into such a dead lethargy, that they could not easily be aroused. Battologia est, sed necessaria verborum redundantia, saith Pintus.
paragraphs.anchor: An end is come, the end is come.

paragraphs.text: Which hitherto lay at the door, {Gen 4:7} sleeping dog sleep, as we say. In the Hebrew there is an elegant alliteration between hakets, "an end," and hekits, "watcheth." See 2Pe 3:3.
paragraphs.anchor: It watcheth for thee.

paragraphs.text: {a} The morning of execution (as Jer 21:12 Psa 101:8 cf. Hos 10:15 Gen 19:23-24), worse than the Sicilian Vespers or the French massacre. Thine utter destruction, bene mane in te irruet, shall be upon thee early, as it was upon Sodom, and as the morning light breaketh in upon those that are fast asleep. Sicut decoctores multa sibi promittunt, interim pereunt. So it befalleth the wicked. {b}
paragraphs.anchor: The morning is come unto thee.

paragraphs.text: Hajom mehumah. "Day" in Hebrew is thought to have its name from the stir and noise that is made in it, the humming noise and bustle of business. A troublesome and tumultuous day is here forethreatened, such as that in Isa 22:5 Zep 1:14-17.
paragraphs.anchor: The day of trouble is near.

paragraphs.text: Not an empty sound, or an echo - resonabilis echo {c} - but a worse matter, that shall do more than beat the air.
paragraphs.anchor: Not the sounding again of the mountains.

paragraphs.text: {a} Visitaberis summo mane, id est mature. - Piscat.
{b} Florulenta felicitas occidit. - Oecol.
{c} Virgil.
See on Eze 5:13.
paragraphs.anchor: Now will I shortly pour out my fury.

paragraphs.text: See on Eze 7:3.
paragraphs.anchor: And I will judge thee, &c.

paragraphs.text: The same as before. Nunquam satis dicitur, quod nunquam satis discitur.
paragraphs.anchor: I will recompense.

paragraphs.text: Think not that I am made all of mercy, or that I will ever serve you for a sinning stock. Ye shall know that I have verbera flogging as well as ubera, plenty and can so set it on as no creature can take it off.
paragraphs.anchor: That I am the Lord that smiteth.

paragraphs.text: Matutina sententia, The decree bringeth forth, {as Zep 2:2} {See Trapp on "Zep 2:2"}
paragraphs.anchor: The morning is gone forth.

paragraphs.text: You have had your floralia, good times and shall shortly have your funeralia, funeral. Nebuchadnezzar (that rod of my wrath) is at hand.
paragraphs.anchor: The rod hath blossomed.

paragraphs.text: And will shortly bring forth, viz., the bitter fruit of your bold rebellion. Not much unlike to this was the almond rod seen by Jeremiah. {Eze 1:11}
paragraphs.anchor: Pride hath budded.

paragraphs.text: Their oppressions speak them most wicked, and will make them most wretched.
paragraphs.anchor: Violence is risen up into a rod of wickedness.

paragraphs.text: Or, Their tumultuous persons, their Thrasos, saith Tremellius, quantumvis circumstrepant famulitio numeroso, with all their train and retinue, that keep a clutter.
paragraphs.anchor: Nor of their multitude.

paragraphs.text: Their dearest friends shall not dare to lament the loss of them, for fear of the enemies who are present would punish it. We read in the Roman history of one Vitia, who was put to death by the command of Tiberius, for that she had lamented Geminus her son executed as a friend to Sejanus. {a}
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall there be wailing for them.

paragraphs.text: {a} Tacit.

Advenit illud tempus, pertigit ilia dies. Let this voice ever sound in the ears of those negligent spirits who cry Cras Domine, tomorrow Lord, wiling away their time as she in Rev 2:21, and so fooling away their own salvation, as those virgins. {Mat 25:1-12}
paragraphs.anchor: The time is come, the day draweth near.

paragraphs.text: He shall have no such great joy of his purchase, since the enemy shall shortly take all, et qui latifundia habuerunt, ne latum pedem retinebunt, and those who have large estates will not keep back enough for a foot, and no man shall be master of his own, nay, not of a molehill.
paragraphs.anchor: Let not the buyer rejoice.

paragraphs.text: Or, Upon all the wealth thereof. To like purpose the apostle in 1Co 7:29; "This, then, I say, brethren, The time is short," or trussed up, contracted. "Let them that have wives be as though they had none, they that weep as though they wept not, they that rejoice as though they rejoiced not, and they that buy as though they possessed not," &c. Rebus non me trado sed commodo, said the wise heathen. {a} Hang loose to all things here below, and labour after that undefiled and unfadable inheritance. {1Pe 1:4-7}
paragraphs.anchor: For wrath is upon all the multitude thereof.

paragraphs.text: {a} Sen.
scil., At the year of jubilee, by reason of the land’s desolation.
paragraphs.anchor: For the seller shall not return

paragraphs.text: Or rather, It shall not return, scil., void and ineffectual, but shall be accomplished.
paragraphs.anchor: Which shall not return.

paragraphs.text: That is but an ill defence. "The spirit of power and of a sound mind" are fitly set together. {2Ti 1:7} Men’s iniquity will be their ruin. Munster rendereth the text thus: For that whenas the vision was to the whole multitude thereof, no man returned, neque ullus propter iniquitatem suam pro anima sua se roberabat; neither did any one (by reason of his iniquity) strengthen himself for his own soul, i.e., use means to escape the just punishment of it.
paragraphs.anchor: Neither shall any strengthen himself in the iniquity of his life.

paragraphs.text: But all to no purpose, since God hath dispirited them (as he did the old Canaanites, the Saxons and Piers in that Victoria Halleluiatica, the Germans against the Hussites in Bohemia, &c.), and struck them with a panic terror, with utter despondency, so that they were feeble and fainthearted, and the strong were become as tow. {Isa 1:31}
paragraphs.anchor: They have blown the trumpet, even to make all ready.

paragraphs.text: No safety can be to such as are pursued by the divine vengeance, called therefore by the Greeks Aδραστεια, because there is no outrunning of it. {a} Of these three judgments (seldom separated) see Eze 42:1-20; Eze 3:1-27; Eze 16:1-63; Eze 17:1-24 Hξει Dωριακος πολεμος και λιμος {β} επ αυτω.
paragraphs.anchor: The sword is without, and the pestilence, &c.

paragraphs.text: {a} Aδραστεια, οτι ουκ αν τις αυτην αποδρασαιτο.
{b} or λοιμος
Here we have the mournful repentance of them that escaped, Fere autem fit ut, malo demure accepto, oculos aperiamus, saith Lavater here.
paragraphs.anchor: But they that escaped of them.

paragraphs.text: All of them mourning, {a} every one for his iniquity.] Thus Hezekiah "mourned as a dove." {Isa 38:14} And we mourn sore like doves, saith the Church; {Isa 59:11} happy if it be every man for his iniquity, and not for the punishment of it only or mainly. See that it be a "sorrow according to God," a sorrow to a "transmentation." {2Co 7:10-11}
{a} äîú eiulantes, ut pueri solent qui virgis coercentur.
As after some grievous disease, or as in extreme cold weather, ye shall not be able to handle your arms, wherein ye so trust. God strengtheneth or weakeneth the arms of either party. {Eze 30:24}
paragraphs.anchor: All hands shall be feeble.

paragraphs.text: Fluent aquis: puta sudore ex gravi angustia, vel potius urina, ex pavore. {a} Not to those that wait upon God. {Isa 40:30-31} Let wicked Thrasos think on this.
paragraphs.anchor: And all knees shall be weak as water.

paragraphs.text: {a} Vulg., Jerome, Septuag.
They shall be a miserable mourning people for a long while.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall also gird themselves with sackcloth.

paragraphs.text: Such heartquake as is in earthquakes - horripilatio.
paragraphs.anchor: Horror shall cover them.

paragraphs.text: Pudor a rebus putidis, {a} - Ashamed they shall be of their doings, ashamed of their disappointments.
paragraphs.anchor: Shame shall be upon all faces.

paragraphs.text: A sign of sorrow among the Jews. The Romans (contrariwise), in times of sorrow, suffered their hair to grow, saith Plutarch; so did Mephibosheth in David’s days.
paragraphs.anchor: And baldness upon all their heads.

paragraphs.text: {a} Scal.

As burdensome, and not beneficial to them {a} Thus Judas threw away his wages of wickedness; and many, on their deathbeds, detest their cursed hoards of ill gotten goods, saying unto them, as once Charles V did, Abite hinc, abite longe, - Away from me, away, away.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall cast their silver in the streets.

paragraphs.text: Shall be for a dunghill, saith the Vulgate; it shall be esteemed, as it is, the guts and garbage of the earth.
paragraphs.anchor: Their gold shall be removed.

paragraphs.text: See Pro 11:4 Zep 1:18 Ecc 5:8, {See Trapp on "Pro 11:4"} {See Trapp on "Zep 1:18"} {See Trapp on "Ecc 5:8"}
paragraphs.anchor: Their silver and their gold.

paragraphs.text: They shall not satisfy {b} their souls.] Silver and gold are not eatable, as Midas found, and the great Caliph of Babylon, whom Haabon the great Khan of Tartary starved to death in the midst of his infinite treasures, which though they were in valour great, and with great care laid together, yet served they him not now to suffice nature best contented with a little. {c}
Their wealth is the occasion of their wickedness, and they are much the worse men for their worldly substance. See Psa 52:7, with the margin; Jer 5:27-28 Luk 16:9; Luk 16:13.
paragraphs.anchor: Because it is the stumblingblock of their iniquity.

paragraphs.text: {a} Ne sit ponderi quod prius fuit luxuriae. - Jerome.
{b} Plato in Cratylo scribit Tantalum dictum esse quas παλαντατον, i.e., infelicissimum
{c} Turkish History, 113.
That is mine ark, saith Junius; or my silver and gold, {Eze 7:10} as others.
paragraphs.anchor: As for the beauty of his ornament.

paragraphs.text: In superbiam posuit, placed it pride, so some render it; they were proud of their abundance - their good and their blood rose together, as the proverb is.
paragraphs.anchor: He set it in majesty.

paragraphs.text: I will - for their ingratitude and abuse my good things - take away mine own and begone, as Hos 2:8-9.
paragraphs.anchor: Therefore have I set it far from them.

paragraphs.text: So he did the pleasant land to be plundered, the sanctuary also to be rifled and ransacked by the Babylonians, Syrians, Romans, &c. See Lam 1:10, {See Trapp on "Lam 1:10"}
paragraphs.anchor: And I will give it into the hands.

paragraphs.text: Sept., To the pests of the earth.
paragraphs.anchor: And to the wicked of the earth.

paragraphs.text: From the Chaldees, that they may spoil at pleasure; or from the Israelites, that they may perish without help.
paragraphs.anchor: My face will I turn also from them.

paragraphs.text: Even the Holy of holies, whereinto none was to enter but the high priest once a year; yet, besides these Babylonian burglars, Heliodorus and Pompey did; but the one fell mad, and the other never prospered after it.
paragraphs.anchor: And they shall pollute my secret place.

paragraphs.text: Effractores; by this name, breach makers, the Jews at this day term our nobles and grandees.
paragraphs.anchor: For the robbers shall enter into it.

paragraphs.text: Which is an emblem of bondage.
paragraphs.anchor: Make a chain.

paragraphs.text: i.e., Capital crimes, unjust sentences, and other deadly evils.
paragraphs.anchor: For the land is full of bloody crimes

paragraphs.text: Velut carnifices; who may plunder you to the life, and take away your lives. {Hab 1:6-7; Hab 1:9} The Jews were bad enough, but the Chaldees were worse, if worse might be; malignants above measure, Poneropolitans, breathing devils. A hard knot must have a harder wedge, as the proverb is.
paragraphs.anchor: Wherefore I will bring the worst of the heathen.

paragraphs.text: I will crush the crests of those potentates, and lay them low. See Isa 14:11-12.
paragraphs.anchor: I will also make the pomp of the strong to cease.

paragraphs.text: Sacella et lararia eorum; their chapels or oratories made in or near unto their houses for divine worship.
paragraphs.anchor: Their holy places shall be defiled.

paragraphs.text: Not εξιλασμος ηκει, Mercy shall come, as the Septuagint ill render it, but utter excision, as when a weaver cutteth the web he hath finished out of the loom. {Isa 38:12}
paragraphs.anchor: Destruction cometh.

paragraphs.text: Of God, but all too late; of the Chaldees, but all in vain; for they were cockatrices, and would not be charmed. {Jer 8:17; Jer 8:15; Jer 12:12; Jer 16:5} Note here how Jeremiah and Ezekiel say the same thing, as being acted by the same spirit.
paragraphs.anchor: They shall seek peace.

paragraphs.text: Aliud ex alio malum; I will heap mischiefs upon them. {Deu 32:23} War is called "evil" or "mischief" by a specialty. {Isa 45:7}
paragraphs.anchor: Mischief shall come upon mischief.

paragraphs.text: sc., Of Nebuchadnezzar’s advance, acts, and achievements.
paragraphs.anchor: And rumour shall be upon rumour

paragraphs.text: As a drowning man catcheth at the sprig of a tree, which before he slighted.
paragraphs.anchor: Then shall they seek a vision of the prophet.

paragraphs.text: Not only prophecy, which is an extraordinary gift, shall fail them, but also the ordinary preaching of God’s Word, and all good advice and provision of human wisdom. And yet this foolish people were wont to soothe up themselves and say, The law shall not perish from the priest, nor wisdom from the ancient. {Jer 18:18}
paragraphs.anchor: But the law shall perish from the priest.

paragraphs.text: Pενθησει; with a funeral mourning, as the Septuagint express it; with a continued mourning, as the Hebrew importeth.
paragraphs.anchor: The king shall mourn.

paragraphs.text: Opplebitur tristitia ad stuporem.
paragraphs.anchor: The prince shall be clothed with desolation.

paragraphs.text: Which they had so often lifted up to vanity.
paragraphs.anchor: And the hands.

paragraphs.text: See Eze 7:3-4; Eze 7:8-9.
paragraphs.anchor: According to their deserts.
